description: ASML, under sustained American pressure over its exports, becomes the focal point of a quiet crisis in EU-US relations. The European Commission begins to explore using its regulatory authority over ASML as a bargaining chip to secure guaranteed access to frontier AI models, testing whether its chokepoint in semiconductor manufacturing can be leveraged for AI sovereignty. The move is legally plausible but diplomatically volatile, and its success depends on cohesion among member states and the credibility of the EU's willingness to resist unilateral pressure.
